title: Apical periodontitis: can the X-ray see it?
topic: Periapical bone loss from canal bacteria can be under way while a 2-D PA still looks normal; CBCT and histology find more lesions.

claims.claim: No bacteria, no lesion (germ-free rats): exposed pulps without bacteria did not form periapical lesions
claims.source: Kakehashi et al., Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol 1965;20:340-9 (PMID 14342926)

claims.claim: The immune response drives bone resorption: macrophages and T cells, then IL-1β, TNF-α and PGE₂
claims.source: Stashenko et al., J Endod 1992;18:422-6 (PMID 9796508); Nair, Crit Rev Oral Biol Med 2004;15:348-81 (PMID 15574679)

claims.claim: RANKL : OPG ratio rises and osteoclasts resorb periapical bone
claims.source: Kawashima et al., Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol Oral Radiol Endod 2007;103:707-11 (PMID 17336108)

claims.claim: Bone is being lost, but the PA can still look normal (small lesion confined to cancellous bone)
claims.source: Gao et al., J Endod 2010;36:1404-9 (PMID 20647106); Kanagasingam et al., Int Endod J 2017;50:417-26 (PMID 27063209)

claims.claim: Early, subtle sign on the PA: apical PDL widening / broken lamina dura
claims.source: Ørstavik et al., Endod Dent Traumatol 1986;2:20-34 (PMID 3457698)

claims.claim: Much clearer once the cortex is involved (classic cadaver study, bur-made defects)
claims.source: Bender & Seltzer, JADA 1961;62:152-60, reprinted J Endod 2003;29:702-6 (PMID 14651274)

claims.claim: Digital PAs: lesion size predicts detection better than cortical involvement
83 dog roots, histology as reference: AP diagnosed in 93% by histology, 84% by CBCT, 71% by PA; the gap is AP missed on PA
claims.source: de Paula-Silva et al., J Endod 2009;35:1009-12 (PMID 19567324)

claims.claim: PA stays first-line; limited-FOV CBCT if signs are contradictory
claims.source: AAE & AAOMR Joint Position Statement, Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol Oral Radiol 2015;120:508-12 (PMID 26346911)

claims.claim: Healing also shows late on radiographs: review at ≥ 1 yr, up to 4 yrs

caption:
A normal PA doesn't mean no lesion.

Canal bacteria trigger the host response: immune cells, IL-1β/TNF-α/PGE₂ and a rising RANKL:OPG ratio drive osteoclastic bone loss.
A small lesion in cancellous bone can stay quiet on a 2-D film. PDL widening may be the first hint; the radiolucency gets much clearer as it grows and reaches the cortex.
83 dog roots vs histology: PA 71%, CBCT 84%, histology 93%.
PA stays first-line; consider limited-FOV CBCT when signs don't add up.

Refs: de Paula-Silva 2009, J Endod; Chang 2020, J Endod; AAE/AAOMR 2015 position statement
Animation is schematic, not to scale.
